**Wire verb `stats adjust`**: Adjust a list of p-values for the false discovery rate with Benjamini-Hochberg, keeping every input position and leaving untested entries out of the family.

# Wraps

- [`MultipleTesting.BenjaminiHochberg`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/0a808fec/mzLib/StatisticalModels/MultipleTesting.cs) in `mzLib/StatisticalModels/MultipleTesting.cs` at mzLib `0a808fec`

# Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stdin` (wire `--stdin`) | `string[]` | required | — | `>= 1 line; each in [0, 1], blank, NA or NaN` | One p-value per line. BLANK LINES ARE KEPT (as in sdrf parse-age) so output row i is line i; one trailing newline does not add a line. A blank, NA or NaN line is a feature that was not tested: it stays null and is not counted in m. A UTF-8 BOM is dropped. |

# Returns

Top-level fields:

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `line_count` | `int` | lines | never | Lines read from stdin; the length of every column. |
| `tested_count` | `int` | p-values | never | m: the finite p-values, the family the adjustment is over. |
| `row_count` | `int` | rows | never | Equal to line\_count. |
| `columns` (wire `column_names`) | `string[]` | — | never | The table's columns. |
| `columns` | `table` | — | never | One row per input line, in order. |
| `caveats` | `string[]` | — | never | Two static caveats. |

Per-row fields (one value per record, in `columns` or each list entry):

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `p_value` | `float` | fraction (0 to 1) | yes: the line was blank, NA or NaN: not tested | The p-value as read. |
| `bh_adjusted` | `float` | fraction (0 to 1) | yes: not tested | min over j &gt;= i of p\_(j) m / j, capped at 1, for the i-th smallest p-value. |

# Errors

| Kind | mzLibRust returns | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | stdin empty; a line that is not a number (other than blank, NA, NaN); a p-value outside \[0, 1\] (mzLib's refusal, reclassified) |
| `correctness` | [`MzLibError::Bridge`](crate::MzLibError::Bridge) | never expected |
| `service_unavailable` | [`MzLibError::ServiceUnavailable`](crate::MzLibError::ServiceUnavailable) | never returned by this verb |

Any call can also fail on the way to mzLib or back, whatever the verb: [`MzLibError::BridgeNotFound`](crate::MzLibError::BridgeNotFound), [`MzLibError::Timeout`](crate::MzLibError::Timeout), [`MzLibError::Protocol`](crate::MzLibError::Protocol) or [`MzLibError::Io`](crate::MzLibError::Io).

# Caveats

- Benjamini-Hochberg controls the false discovery rate among the features tested. It is not a target-decoy q-value for identifications.
- m is the number of finite p-values. Leave a line blank, or write NA, for a feature that was not tested rather than writing 1, which would enlarge the family.
- stats fit already reports bh\_adjusted per coefficient; use this verb for p-values from anywhere else.
